title.en: Five dead, 41 missing, after Indonesia ferry catches fire
title.zh: 印度尼西亚渡轮起火，五人死亡，41人失踪

summary.en: A ferry carrying 271 people caught fire off Madura island in Indonesia, resulting in five deaths and 41 individuals reported missing.
summary.zh: 一艘载有271人的渡轮在印度尼西亚马都拉岛附近起火，造成5人死亡，另有41人失踪。

body.en:
Five people have been found dead and 41 are missing after an Indonesian ferry carrying at least 250 people caught fire while at sea, officials say.

The captain of the ship reported the fire - off Madura island - as the vessel sailed from the country's second-largest city, Surabaya in East Java, to Makassar in South Sulawesi, according to Basarnas, the National Search and Rescue Agency.

Footage played by local Indonesian news outlet iNews shows large numbers of people in life jackets on what appears to be a lifeboat.

Other clips show people climbing down from the ferry that has flames and plumes of smoke coming from the top of the vessel.

Basarnas posted a video to its TikTok, with a statement saying at 08:24 (02:24 GMT) the Surabaya Search and Rescue office received information that passenger ship KMP Mutiara Sentosa 2 was on fire.

"Based on information from the shipping company, the fire occurred at around 06:00-07:00 (00:00-01:00 GMT)."

Later, Basarnas said it got confirmation the ferry "was almost entirely engulfed in flames" as "passengers held on in the ship's bridge and bow while awaiting rescue".

In some of the footage, can be seen jumping into the sea, with crowds of people in life jackets gathering and lifebuoys being thrown to some before they are carried into a rescue ship.
body.zh: 官员称，一艘载有271人的印度尼西亚渡轮在海上起火，已造成5人死亡、41人失踪。 据国家搜救机构巴萨纳斯称，当该船从该国第二大城市东爪哇的泗水驶往南苏拉威西岛的望加锡时，船长在马都拉岛附近报告了火灾。 印度尼西亚当地新闻媒体 iNews 播放的视频显示，似乎是一艘救生艇上有大量穿着救生衣的人。 其他视频显示，人们从渡轮上爬下来，渡轮顶部冒出火焰和浓烟。 此突发新闻报道正在更新，更多详细信息将很快发布。请刷新页面以获得完整版本。 您可以通过 BBC 新闻应用程序在智能手机或平板电脑上接收突发新闻。您还可以在外部 X 上关注 @BBCBreaking 以获取最新警报。

reflection.en: News of lives lost and missing at sea brings profound sorrow and reminds us of life's fragility. In moments of such deep grief, we remember that Yahweh himself wept at the loss of a friend, showing us that tears are a natural and sacred response to suffering. May those affected find comfort in knowing their pain is seen and shared.
reflection.zh: 海上生命逝去和失踪的消息带来深切的悲痛，提醒我们生命的脆弱。在如此深重的悲伤时刻，我们记得雅伟也曾为朋友的离世而哭泣，这表明眼泪是对苦难自然而神圣的回应。愿受影响的人们在他们的痛苦被看见和分担中找到慰藉。

verse.textEn: Jesus wept.
verse.textZh: 耶稣哭了。

title.en: Moscow restaurant blast a 'brutal terror attack,' mayor says
title.zh: 莫斯科市长称餐厅爆炸为“残酷恐怖袭击”

summary.en: An explosion outside an upscale Moscow restaurant at Kudrinskaya Square, described by Mayor Sergei Sobyanin as a "brutal terror attack," resulted in fatalities. The mayor vowed that those responsible would be punished, though many questions about the incident remain unanswered.
summary.zh: 莫斯科市长谢尔盖·索比亚宁称，库德林斯卡亚广场一家高档餐厅外发生的致命爆炸是“残酷的恐怖袭击”，并承诺将惩罚肇事者。然而，关于此事件的许多问题仍未解决。

body.en:
The deadly explosion outside an upscale Moscow restaurant at Kudrinskaya Square was a "brutal terror attack," Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said, promising the perpetrators would be punished. But many questions remain.

An explosion at a restaurant in central Moscow killed at least three people, including the suspected bomber on Saturday night, authorities said.

"Law enforcement agencies are investigating the circumstances of the incident. Those responsible for this crime will certainly be found and face the punishment they deserve," he said in an online post on Sunday.

Russia's Anti-Terrorism Committee said a woman carrying  "a homemade explosive device" tried to enter the restaurant on Kudrinskaya Square but was stopped by a security guard.

The device exploded at the entrance, killing the woman, the guard and a restaurant patron.

State news agency RIA Novosti reported that at least 21 other people were injured in the blast, which occurred shortly before 8 p.m. local time (5 p.m. UTC).

The restaurant's website said the venue had been closed on Saturday for a private event.

Heavily armed law enforcement officers sealed off the area and launched an investigation.

Authorities did not immediately identify those they believed to be behind the attack.

Russia has faced several attacks since the start of the war in Ukraine in 2022. They blamed a ‌series of assassinations and attempted killings on Kyiv. Russian officials have yet to comment on any possible Ukrainian involvement into the Kudrinskaya Square blast.

However, Ukraine used drones to attack other parts of Russia on Saturday evening and early on Sunday, including a bombing which targeted an apartment block and killed two in the city Engels, some 900 kilometers (560 miles) southeast of Moscow.

Russia's Defense Ministry also said Kyiv struck a warehouse belonging to Wildberries, a major online retailer in Russia, with the Ukrainian drones hitting a site in the Samara Oblast, deep inside Russian territory. Regional Governor Vyacheslav Fedorishchev said it was not immediately clear if there were any casualties.

Russian officials also reported over a 100 Ukrainian strikes in the Belgorod Oblast, which borders Ukraine. They said Kyiv forces used artillery, rocket launchers, and drones, leaving 14 people injured.

Over 200 Ukrainian drones have allegedly been shot down during the wave of attacks.

Meanwhile, at least one person was killed and seven wounded in the Russian attack on Ukraine's Kherson, with the attack involving artillery fire.

In Dnipro, seven passengers were wounded in a drone strike on a minibus, with the regional military administrator Oleksandr Hanzha describing it as a "deliberate and cynical attack on civilians."

reflection.en: In the wake of such a brutal act, the natural human response can be to seek retribution in kind. Yet, Yahweh's word calls us to a different path, reminding us not to be overcome by evil, but to actively overcome evil with good. This challenges us to seek justice and peace in ways that break cycles of violence rather than perpetuate them.
reflection.zh: 在如此残酷的行径之后，人类自然的反应可能是以牙还牙。然而，雅伟的话语呼召我们走一条不同的道路，提醒我们不要被恶所胜，反要以善胜恶。这挑战我们以打破而非延续暴力循环的方式寻求公义与和平。

verse.textEn: Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
verse.textZh: 你不可为恶所胜，反要以善胜恶。

title.en: Trump climbs down on Iran strikes in expectation of ‘rapidly’ reaching a deal
title.zh: 特朗普在预期“迅速”达成协议后取消对伊朗的打击

summary.en: US President Donald Trump announced the cancellation of planned military strikes against Iran, citing the expectation of quickly reaching a deal on its nuclear program and the full opening of the Strait of Hormuz. He also stated that the delay was in response to requests from Iran and other regional countries.
summary.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普宣布取消对伊朗的军事打击计划，理由是预期将“迅速”达成一项关于其核计划和霍尔木兹海峡全面开放的协议。他还表示，这一推迟也是应伊朗和该地区其他国家的要求。

body.en: US president claims delay is also in response to requests from Iran and other countries in the region Donald Trump has said he cancelled planned military strikes against Iran on the basis of “rapidly” reaching a deal on its nuclear programme and the full opening of the strait of Hormuz. The US president paused the strikes in expectation of a breakthrough and in response to requests from Iran and other countries in the region, he claimed on his Truth Social platform on Saturday. verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.

title.en: Trump cancels Iran strikes subject to deal being made 'rapidly'
title.zh: 特朗普称他将取消对伊朗的袭击，前提是协议能“迅速”达成

summary.en: The US president announced the cancellation of planned military strikes on Iran, stating that the decision was made after Iran and other Middle Eastern nations requested a halt to allow for a rapid agreement on a deal. He claimed the "perimeters" of a deal had already been agreed upon.
summary.zh: 美国总统宣布取消对伊朗的军事打击计划，称此决定是在伊朗及其他中东国家要求暂停袭击，以便迅速达成协议后作出的。他声称协议的“范围”已经达成一致。

body.en:
Donald Trump says he has cancelled strikes against Iran, provided a deal is struck "rapidly" with the country.

In a post on Truth Social, the US president said he had been asked by Iran and other countries in the Middle East to "hold off" on any attack as the "perimeters" of a deal had been agreed.

Trump's comments came after reports that the US and Israel may have been planning new, intense strikes on Iran.

It is not the first time that Trump has issued apocalyptic warnings, only to subsequently insist that diplomacy was being given a chance.

Iran's semi-official Mehr news agency denied that Tehran had asked the US to hold off on further military action, saying Trump's claims were "nothing but a new lie".

Iran's acting Defence Minister Majid Ibn al-Reza said Tehran viewed every threat from its adversaries as "real and credible" even if it formed part of psychological warfare.

The raised tones followed reports in the US media that the US and Israel were planning what would be one of the harshest bombing campaigns to date against energy infrastructure targets in Iran.

The plan came up during Trump's cabinet meeting on Friday, sources told CBS News, the BBC's News partner in the US.

The US government had also urged Americans across the Middle East to be alert and ready to leave "should there be escalation" in the region.

In his post on Saturday, Trump said the US was "locked and loaded and ready to go against the Islamic Republic of Iran, at levels of Military Terror, Strength, and Power not seen since World War II".

He said cancelling the attack would be "for the future benefit of the world and, likewise, the survival of a successful and prosperous Iran".

Back on 7 April, the US president warned that "a whole civilisation will die tonight" if Iran refused to engage in peace talks. He threatened to destroy civilian infrastructure and power plants, a move that many said would be a war crime.

That threat did result in historic face-to-face talks in Pakistan, led by Vice President JD Vance.

For supporters of the president, it was vindication. Bellicose threats - often referred to as the "Madman Theory" - resulted in talks with the Iranians.

The issue with that view, however, is that those talks ended without a deal. There were simply too many competing red lines that could not be reconciled, even with the threat of civilisation erasure.

During the Friday meeting, CBS News reported Trump was heard saying while reporters were still in the room: "We'll be hitting them [Iranians] very hard. At some point, they're going to say, 'We just can't take it anymore.'"

A day later, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed Bin Salman had a call with Trump, aimed at reducing regional tensions, the kingdom's official SPA press agency reported.

reflection.en: At moments of heightened tension, the decision to step back from conflict and pursue dialogue is a profound act. Yahweh blesses those who actively work to bridge divides and prevent violence, for they reflect His own desire for reconciliation. May leaders everywhere be guided towards paths of peace, seeking understanding over confrontation.

verse.textEn: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.

title.en: Five dead, 41 missing in Indonesia ferry fire
title.zh: 印度尼西亚渡轮火灾致五人死亡，41人失踪

summary.en: Five people have died and 41 are missing after a passenger ferry caught fire off the coast of South Sulawesi, Indonesia, marking the country's second ferry accident in two months.
summary.zh: 印度尼西亚南苏拉威西省望加锡市附近发生一起客运渡轮火灾，造成五人死亡，41人失踪，这是该国两个月内发生的第二起渡轮事故。

body.en:
Five people have been killed and 41 are ‌still missing after a ‌ferry caught fire off Indonesia's Madura island, the country's search and rescue agency says .

⁠The Mutiara Santos 2 was carrying 271 passengers and crew members, with 225 people rescued, said the regional Surabaya Search and Rescue Agency on Sunday evening. A search ⁠and ‌rescue operation is ongoing.

The ferry ‌was heading from Surabaya in East Java province to Makassar city in South Sulawesi.

It was unclear how it caught ‌fire. Madura island is located off the northeastern coast of Java. Java and Madura are next to Bali.

Basarnas, Indonesia's National Search and Rescue Agency also said some passengers jumped into the sea and were picked up by a nearby ship. Four other vessels were on standby near the ferry but could not approach because of the risk posed by flammable material on the ferry.

The captain had called the ferry company to report the fire but had not been in contact since, Basarnas added.

A larger rescue operation was heading to the site from Surabaya, a six-hour journey from the site of the disaster, Basarnas said.

"Based on preliminary reports from the field, passengers are waiting to be evacuated by the vessels in the vicinity of the incident site," Muhammad Masyhud, a senior official at the Ministry of Transportation, said in a statement.

"The safety of passengers and crew is our top priority. We are continuously coordinating with all relevant parties to ensure that the evacuation process can proceed quickly, safely, and effectively."

Marine accidents are a regular occurrence in Indonesia , an archipelago of more than 17,000 islands, partly due to lax safety standards and unpredictable weather.

A ferry transporting more than 70 people sank last month while sailing near Selayar, a small tropical island south of the much larger Sulawesi. At least four people were found dead, and 14 others remained missing until the end of the search operation.

body.zh: 印度尼西亚搜救机构称，一艘渡轮在印度尼西亚马都拉岛附近起火，已造成 5 人死亡、41 人失踪。 泗水地区搜救机构周日晚表示，Mutiara Santos 2 号载有 271 名乘客和船员，其中 225 人获救。搜救行动正在进行中。 该渡轮正从东爪哇省泗水前往南苏拉威西岛望加锡市。 目前尚不清楚它是如何着火的。马都拉岛位于爪哇岛东北海岸附近。爪哇岛和马都拉岛紧邻巴厘岛。 印尼国家搜救机构巴萨纳斯也表示，一些乘客跳入海中，被附近的一艘船只救起。另外四艘船只在渡轮附近待命，但由于渡轮上的易燃材料构成风险而无法靠近。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 巴萨纳斯补充说，船长曾致电渡轮公司报告火灾情况，但此后就没有再联系过。 巴萨纳斯说，更大规模的救援行动正从泗水前往现场，距离灾难现场有六个小时的路程。 交通部高级官员穆罕默德·马西胡德在一份声明中表示：“根据现场的初步报告，乘客正在事发地点附近等待船只疏散。” “乘客和机组人员的安全是我们的首要任务。我们正在与所有相关方不断协调，以确保疏散过程能够快速、安全、有效地进行。” 印度尼西亚是一个由 17,000 多个岛屿组成的群岛，海上事故经常发生，部分原因是安全标准松懈和天气变化莫测。 上个月，一艘载有 70 多人的渡轮在塞拉雅附近航行时沉没。塞拉雅是面积大得多的苏拉威西岛以南的一个热带小岛。至少 4 人被发现死亡，另有 14 人在搜寻行动结束前仍下落不明。 如需了解 SBS 新闻的最新动态，请下载我们的应用程序并订阅我们的时事通讯。

reflection.en: This tragic news of lives lost and missing at sea reminds us of the profound sorrow that accompanies such events. Yet, the Scriptures offer a future hope where Yahweh himself will wipe away every tear, and death, sorrow, crying, and pain will be no more. This promise anchors our hearts even amidst present grief.
reflection.zh: 这起海上渡轮火灾造成人员伤亡和失踪的悲剧性新闻，提醒我们此类事件所带来的深切悲痛。然而，圣经提供了一个未来的盼望，那时雅伟将亲自擦去所有的眼泪，死亡、悲伤、哭泣和痛苦都将不复存在。这个应许在当前的悲痛中为我们的心提供了锚定。

verse.textEn: He will wipe every tear from their eyes. There will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain.
verse.textZh: 神要擦去他们一切的眼泪；不再有死亡，也不再有悲哀、哭号、疼痛。

title.en: US officials focus on identification and rapid action as measles cases rise
title.zh: 随着麻疹病例上升，美国官员专注于识别和快速行动

summary.en: Authorities in Delaware tackle cluster with vaccination and contract tracing – but field has been weakened by cuts Measles outbreaks are igniting throughout the United States as the nation passes the highest case count in 30 years – putting greater pressure on state and local...
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en: Authorities in Delaware tackle cluster with vaccination and contract tracing – but field has been weakened by cuts Measles outbreaks are igniting throughout the United States as the nation passes the highest case count in 30 years – putting greater pressure on state and local health departments and highlighting the importance of early identification and quick action. The US has officially surpassed last year’s tally of measles cases, reaching 2,371 confirmed infections by the end of July. Those numbers have been driven by clusters in Arizona, South Carolina, and Utah – but in times of high transmission, outbreaks elsewhere become more likely. And with decreasing vaccination rates across the country, these sparks are falling on increasingly dry timber. Continue reading...
body.zh: 特拉华州当局通过疫苗接种和接触者追踪来应对聚集性感染，但由于削减力度，麻疹疫情在美国各地爆发，病例数达到了 30 年来的最高水平，这给州和地方卫生部门带来了更大的压力，并凸显了早期识别和快速行动的重要性。截至 7 月底，美国麻疹病例总数已正式超过去年，确诊人数达到 2,371 例。这些数字是由亚利桑那州、南卡罗来纳州和犹他州的感染群推动的，但在传播率高的时期，其他地方爆发疫情的可能性更大。随着全国疫苗接种率的下降，这些火花正落在日益干燥的木材上。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This story draws attention to peace-making and restraint. Matthew 5:9 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with mercy, truth, and restraint, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到和平与克制。Matthew 5:9提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以怜悯、真实与节制来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.
verse.textZh: 使人和睦的人有福了，因为他们必称为神的儿子。

title.en: It was about the adventure, says fastest runner to cross the Alps
title.zh: 穿越阿尔卑斯山最快的跑步者说，这是关于冒险的

summary.en: Sophie Woods ran the Via Alpina through storms, heat of up to 37C and dodged floods and wildfires across eight countries.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Runner Sophie Woods has become the fastest person to complete a 2,000km (1242 miles) ultramarathon across the Alps.

Woods ran the Via Alpina through storms, heat of up to 37C and dodged floods and wildfires across eight countries.

"Through the whole thing, I was only ever thinking about the day, the hour, the sort of minute that I was in", the runner told BBC Breakfast.

The previous record was 35 days and Woods did it in just 29, crediting ice cream slushies for helping her power through.
body.zh: 跑步者索菲·伍兹 (Sophie Woods) 成为穿越阿尔卑斯山 2,000 公里（1242 英里）超级马拉松最快的人。 伍兹冒着暴风雨和高达 37 摄氏度的高温跑过阿尔皮纳大道 (Via Alpina)，并在八个国家躲避了洪水和野火。 这位跑步者告诉英国广播公司早餐频道：“在整个过程中，我只想到我所处的那一天、那一小时、那一分钟。” 之前的纪录是 35 天，伍兹只用了 29 天就打破了这一纪录，这归功于冰淇淋泥帮助她克服了困难。

reflection.en: This story draws attention to compassion for vulnerable people. Galatians 6:2 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with practical compassion and welcome, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到对脆弱群体的怜悯。Galatians 6:2提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以具体的怜悯与接纳来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: Truly I tell you, whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for me.
verse.textZh: 我实在告诉你们，这些事你们既做在我这弟兄中一个最小的身上，就是做在我身上了。

title.en: Three killed after bomb detonated at Moscow restaurant, state media say
title.zh: 国家媒体称，莫斯科餐厅发生炸弹爆炸，三人死亡

summary.en: Security officials reported that three people were killed after a bomb was detonated at a Moscow restaurant. State media indicated that a woman attempted to enter the establishment with explosives but was intercepted by a security guard.
summary.zh: 据国家媒体报道，一枚炸弹在莫斯科一家餐厅引爆，造成三人死亡。安全官员称，一名女子试图携带爆炸物进入餐厅，但被一名保安拦下。

body.en:
At least three people have been killed and 21 injured after a homemade explosive device was detonated at an Italian restaurant in Moscow, Russian state media reports, quoting security officials.

The blast happened at about 20:00 local time (17:00 GMT) on Kudrinskaya square near the city centre.

The National Anti-Terrorist Committee said a woman carrying the explosives tried to enter the restaurant but was stopped by a security guard.

The device detonated, killing the woman, the guard and a visitor to the Balzi Rossi restaurant, which had been holding a private function.

Authorities have not said who they believe was the target, but many Muscovites will suspect a link to the war in Ukraine.

The mayor of Moscow, Sergei Sobyanin, said the blast was "a cruel act of terror which took human lives".

He gave no other details, other than to say law-enforcement agencies were working to establish what had happened.

In recent years, several senior Russian military figures have been assassinated in and around the Russian capital. Moscow has blamed Kyiv for those attacks.

Initial reports said the blast happened in the establishment's kitchen but the restaurant later issued a statement saying "there was a problem outside".

The restaurant is located in one of Moscow's famous Stalin-era skyscrapers, with roads around the square briefly closed.

Dozens of cyclists had been gathering nearby for an evening ride through the city but the event was cancelled.

Video released by Russia's RIA news agency showed heavily armed law enforcement officers at the scene, which had been closed off to members of the public.

The Balzi Rossi restaurant apologised on social media for its initial post after the explosion, saying it had been removed "as it was highly inappropriate given the circumstances".

State media reported that it had originally posted on Instagram that everything was safe on the premises.

The restaurant said it had taken measures to ensure it would not happen again, and said staff were focused on assisting guests and emergency services at the time.
body.zh: 俄罗斯官方媒体援引安全官员的话报道称，莫斯科一家意大利餐厅发生自制爆炸装置引爆事件，造成至少 3 人死亡、21 人受伤。 爆炸发生在当地时间 20:00 左右（格林威治标准时间 17:00），地点位于市中心附近的库德林斯卡亚广场。 国家反恐委员会表示，一名携带爆炸物的妇女试图进入餐厅，但被保安拦住。 该装置爆炸，导致该名女子、警卫和一名前往 Balzi Rossi 餐厅的客人死亡，该餐厅当时正在举办私人活动。 当局尚未透露他们认为目标是谁，但许多莫斯科人怀疑这与乌克兰战争有关。 近年来，多位俄罗斯高级军事人物在俄罗斯首都及周边地区遭到暗杀。莫斯科将这些袭击归咎于基辅。 最初的报道称爆炸发生在餐厅的厨房，但餐厅后来发表声明称“外面出现了问题”。 该餐厅位于莫斯科著名的斯大林时代摩天大楼之一，广场周围的道路曾短暂封闭。 数十名骑自行车的人聚集在附近，打算晚上骑车穿过城市，但活动被取消了。 俄罗斯通讯社发布的视频显示，现场有全副武装的执法人员，现场已禁止公众进入。

reflection.en: Acts of violence like this remind us of the destructive power of evil in the world. In the face of such darkness, Yahweh calls us not to be overcome by evil, but to actively seek ways to overcome evil with good. This path requires courage and a steadfast commitment to peace, even amidst tragedy.
reflection.zh: 这样的暴力行为提醒我们世间邪恶的破坏力。面对这样的黑暗，雅伟呼召我们不要被邪恶所胜，而是要积极寻求以善胜恶的方法。这条道路需要勇气，以及即使在悲剧中也要坚定不移地致力于和平。

verse.textEn: Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
verse.textZh: 你不可为恶所胜，反要以善胜恶。

title.en: How Spain's migrant crisis created a political storm - whipped up by social media
title.zh: 西班牙移民危机如何引发政治风暴——社交媒体推波助澜

summary.en: The Ceuta crossings have intensified Europe's political divisions regarding migration, with social media exacerbating the sensitive issue.
summary.zh: 休达边境的移民潮在欧洲引发了政治风暴，暴露了在敏感移民问题上的分歧，社交媒体加剧了这一局面。

body.en:
Most of the tens of thousands of migrants who swam into the Spanish exclave of Ceuta on Thursday have now returned to Morocco, escorted to the border by Spanish soldiers and police.

But the extraordinary surge of arrivals has left at least 72 people dead, their bodies pulled from the sea where they floated alongside abandoned rubber rings and flippers.

This week's events have also shaken Europe politically, once again exposing divisions over the sensitive issue of migration.

And they've left lingering questions about what sparked the sudden influx: whether social media posts promising an easy path to Europe just went viral or this was something more deliberate, even organised.

Whatever the cause, Spain's socialist prime minister is angry with the response.

Pedro Sanchez has hit out at some in the EU for "attacking" Spain in this crisis, playing politics instead of showing support.

Fratelli d'Italia, the hard-right party of Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, had been quick to post images of migrants racing through the streets of Ceuta.

"This is the Sanchez model the Italian left wing likes so much," the caption crowed.

Meloni then announced she was suspending Italy's Schengen agreement with Spain that allows for the free movement of people, citing a security threat.

The way Spain sees it, the crisis has been contained and Ceuta is not in the Schengen zone so Moroccan migrants were never going to head for mainland Europe, unchecked.

But she faces elections next year with her coalition losing ground to a new and virulently anti-immigrant party. This was a chance to sound tough herself and claw back votes and she leaped on it.

Meloni's call for an urgent meeting of interior ministers to be held on Tuesday was signed by almost two dozen EU heads of state, calling for the elimination of all policies that could be "pull factors" to Europe.

Above all, they mean Spain's controversial move to allow hundreds of thousands of undocumented migrants apply for residence and work permits and "regularise" their status.

But those who flocked to the beaches of Ceuta this week were not heading to sign up for a campaign that's already closed.

Sanchez himself points instead to a recent ruling by Spain's Supreme Court: it said those who enter by sea cannot be pushed back immediately.

The prime minister argues that was misrepresented by smugglers to promise an easy path to Europe.

The crowd heading for Ceuta didn't need to pay smugglers, though, because most were Moroccan and the route is well known.

Migrants have shown social media posts to reporters with people shouting that "Spain is Open" and jumping into the sea.

Multiple accounts we've checked ourselves show young people in wetsuits and flippers, or filming themselves already swimming, mixed with...
body.zh: 周四涌入西班牙飞地休达的数万名移民中的大多数现已在西班牙士兵和警察的护送下返回摩洛哥。 但涌入的人数激增，导致至少 72 人死亡，他们的尸体与废弃的橡胶圈和脚蹼一起漂浮在海上。 本周的事件也在政治上震动了欧洲，再次暴露了在敏感的移民问题上的分歧。 他们留下了一个挥之不去的问题，即是什么引发了突然涌入的人潮：社交媒体上承诺通往欧洲的便捷道路的帖子是否只是病毒式传播，还是这是经过深思熟虑、甚至有组织的。 无论出于何种原因，西班牙社会党首相都对这种反应感到愤怒。 佩德罗·桑切斯猛烈抨击欧盟一些人在这场危机中“攻击”西班牙，玩弄政治而不是表示支持。 意大利兄弟会（Fratelli d'Italia）是总理乔治亚·梅洛尼（Giorgia Meloni）领导的极右翼政党，该党很快就发布了移民在休达街道上奔跑的照片。 “这就是意大利左翼非常喜欢的桑切斯模式，”标题欢呼道。 梅洛尼随后宣布，她以安全威胁为由，暂停意大利与西班牙允许人员自由流动的申根协议。 在西班牙看来，危机已经得到遏制，而且休达也不在申根区，因此摩洛哥移民永远不会不受限制地前往欧洲大陆。 但她面临明年的选举，她的联盟将输给一个新的、恶毒的反移民政党。这是一个让自己听起来强硬并夺回选票的机会，她抓住了这个机会。 梅洛尼呼吁周二召开内政部长紧急会议，这一呼吁得到了近二十位欧盟国家元首的签署，呼吁取消所有可能对欧洲产生“拉动因素”的政策。 最重要的是，他们指的是西班牙允许数十万无证移民申请居留和工作许可证并“规范”他们的身份的有争议的举措。 但本周涌入休达海滩的人们并不打算报名参加已经结束的活动。 桑切斯本人则引用了西班牙最高法院最近的一项裁决：该裁决称，不能立即将通过海路入境的人驱逐。 首相辩称，走私者歪曲了这一点，承诺提供一条通往欧洲的便捷道路。 不过，前往休达的人群不需要付钱给走私者，因为大多数是摩洛哥人，而且路线众所周知。 移民向记者展示了社交媒体帖子，人们高喊“西班牙开放”并跳入海中。 我们检查过的多个账户显示，年轻人穿着潜水衣和脚蹼，或者拍摄自己已经游泳的样子，混合着……

reflection.en: The political storm surrounding migration often reveals deep societal divisions, amplified by social media. Yahweh's ancient command reminds us to treat the stranger residing among us as one of our own, loving them as ourselves. This principle calls for compassion and unity, even amidst complex challenges, rather than allowing fear or prejudice to divide.
reflection.zh: 围绕移民的政治风暴常常揭示出深刻的社会分歧，并被社交媒体放大。雅伟古老的诫命提醒我们，要善待居住在我们土地上的陌生人，视他们如同本地人，爱他们如同爱自己。这一原则呼唤我们在复杂的挑战中保持怜悯和合一，而不是让恐惧或偏见造成分裂。

verse.textEn: When a foreigner resides among you in your land, do not mistreat them. The foreigner residing among you must be treated as your native-born. Love them as yourself, for you were foreigners in Egypt.
verse.textZh: 若有外人在你们国中和你同居，就不可欺负他。和你们同居的外人，你们要看他如本地人一样，并要爱他如己，因为你们在埃及地也作过寄居的。

title.en: Relentless UK heatwaves turn ‘green and pleasant land’ brown
title.zh: 英格兰和威尔士在持续热浪后，七月将成为有记录以来最干旱的月份

summary.en: Southern England and the whole of Wales are experiencing an official drought, with July set to be the driest on record. The region received only 1% of its long-term average rainfall last month, a situation climate scientists attribute to extreme heat intensified by the climate crisis.
summary.zh: 英格兰南部和整个威尔士正经历官方干旱，七月有望成为有记录以来最干旱的月份。上个月，该地区仅获得了长期平均降雨量的1%，气候科学家将此归因于气候危机加剧的极端高温。

body.en: Visible impact of warming climate is impossible to ignore across landscapes that have been starved of rainfall Half of England and the whole of Wales are officially in drought and July is set to be the driest month on record as extreme heat intensified by the climate crisis continues to grip the UK and Europe this summer. The announcements this week by England’s Environment Agency and Natural Resources Wales mark the third such event over the past five years, and come in the wake of four record-breaking heatwaves since May which have fuelled huge wildfires and left farmers, wildlife and protected habitats running out of water. Continue reading...
body.zh: 气候科学家敦促更好的规划，因为上个月英格兰南部的降雨量仅为长期平均降雨量的 1%。英格兰的一半和整个威尔士正式处于干旱状态，由于今年夏天气候危机加剧的极端高温继续席卷英国和欧洲，7 月将成为有记录以来最干旱的月份。英格兰环境署和威尔士自然资源部本周宣布的消息是过去五年中第三次发生此类事件，自五月份以来发生了四次破纪录的热浪，这些热浪引发了巨大的野火，导致农民、野生动物和受保护的栖息地缺水。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The news of record drought and relentless heatwaves reminds us that creation itself groans under the weight of environmental distress. As Yahweh's stewards, we are called to listen to these cries and respond with wisdom and care for the world entrusted to us.
reflection.zh: 创纪录的干旱和持续的热浪提醒我们，受环境困扰，受造界本身也在呻吟。作为雅伟的管家，我们蒙召倾听这些呼声，并以智慧和关怀回应我们所受托管理的世界。

verse.textEn: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.
verse.textZh: 我们知道，一切受造之物一同叹息、劳苦，直到如今。

title.en: Poland: Prime Minister Tusk defies anti-Ukrainian violence
title.zh: 波兰：图斯克总理蔑视反乌克兰暴力

summary.en: Anti-Ukrainian sentiment in Poland is on the rise, with numerous attacks against refugees from the war in Ukraine. Prime Minister Donald Tusk has spoken out against the violence and warned of the danger from Russia.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Anti-Ukrainian sentiment in Poland is on the rise, with numerous attacks against refugees from the war in Ukraine. Prime Minister Donald Tusk has spoken out against the violence and warned of the danger from Russia.

The Polish leader didn't mince his words. "We must wage a resolute fight against this violence, because thugs, hooligans, and this culture of violence are becoming increasingly brazen and insolent — and also because they have received political support," Donald Tusk said on Tuesday, before a Polish cabinet meeting in Warsaw. The liberal-conservative prime minister said he deplored the fact that "more and more such incidents" are taking place all over Poland .

Tusk's comments came in response to an incident in Wroclaw two days earlier, in which three Polish men brutally beat up a young Ukrainian man and his girlfriend on the street. Cellphone videos show the attackers kicking the Ukrainian man as he lies on the ground. The woman was also hit, sustaining injuries to her neck and ear.

The attack came after an argument in a shop; the attackers took exception to the couple's Ukrainian accents. Polish police acted swiftly: Two of the attackers, both of whom have previous convictions, are already in custody, and a third is being sought.

Tusk warned that such incidents negatively impact Poland's image abroad. The country's reputation was greatly enhanced by its willingness to provide assistance after the start of Russia's full-scale war against Ukraine . This could be destroyed, said Tusk, "if we allow thugs, hooligans and common criminals to beat and humiliate people just because they have a slightly different accent."

Poland provided military and humanitarian assistance to its neighbor from the very beginning of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. It took in more than one million refugees from the war, and around 1.5 million Ukrainians are currently living in Poland. The majority of them work, pay taxes, and contribute to the Polish economy.

But four and a half years after the start of the war, the mood in Poland has changed. More and more often, Ukrainians are being verbally and physically attacked in public. Last Wednesday a Polish manager on a construction site in Skawina, near Krakow, was filmed aggressively insulting Ukrainian workers. In another incident on a local train near Warsaw, two drunken men shouted verbal abuse at a Ukrainian passenger. On July 11, a man on a bus in Bielsko-Biala insulted and threatened two Ukrainian girls who were trying to take a selfie. Even schoolchildren, including teenagers at a playground, have fallen victim to the new climate of hate.

title.en: On the front line of Europe's battle against wildfires
title.zh: 欧洲抗击野火前线

summary.en: French firefighters successfully contained a massive blaze, allowing nearly 200,000 evacuated residents to return home. However, experts warn that Europe's wildfire season, intensified by climate change, is expected to continue.
summary.zh: 法国消防员成功扑灭了一场大火，近20万撤离居民得以返回家园。然而，专家警告称，受气候影响，欧洲的野火季节远未结束。

body.en:
French firefighters have won out over a massive blaze, with almost 200,000 evacuees returning home. But Europe's climate-fueled wildfire season is far from over.

The signal to move comes suddenly — and within a minute or so the fire truck is full and speeding off into the distance, a cloud of orange dust swirling in its wake. "There's always a bit of adrenaline when you get the call," marine firefighter Julien says. "But we're trained; we're prepared."

Maitre Julien — whom DW can only identity by rank and first name — is part of Marseille-based battalion deployed to France's Gironde region to tackle a wildfire which prompted the largest evacuations in the country since World War II.

Some 264 firefighters were injured in the fight against the Gironde fire, four of whom lost their lives. In nearby towns, French flags still fly at half mast to mark the loss. "It's always on our mind," Lieutenant Damien, another marine firefighter, explains as his team members haul the firehose out behind him.

Letitia, a firefighter and medic, said she tries to ask how colleagues are feeling "without being too intrusive."

"It's the fatigue above all," she says when asked about the most common problem affecting her colleagues. "They're sleeping very little."

"Do you see all all of that?" Maitre Julien asks, gesturing out the car window as he drives past rows of blackened trees and swathes of scorched earth at the roadside. "All of that's already burned. But you can see small peels of smoke here and there. We absolutely have to extinguish those so fires don't restart."

When Julien pulls up at another hotspot, the risk of flare-ups comes sharply into focus: The air smells burned and a cloud of white smoke fills the sky. Within about 20 minutes, the smoke turns thick and black, and the fire — previously under control — was visible burning bright again through the trees.

Here by the firefighters' side are improvised teams of local volunteers — farmers and tradesmen and women who took it upon themselves to use their tractors or vans or four-by-fours to transport water to firefighters on the front line, and often head into the blazes themselves without proper protective gear or training.

"We're here because we're needed. And because we want to help," Steven Page, one volunteer, told DW. Maitre Julien said they played a "primordial" role, saving firefighters "precious time" in the fight.

At times, firefighters said, this felt like a "David and Goliath" battle. But they came out on top. By Saturday, France's Interior Ministry declared the fire was no longer progressing. Most of the 220,000 evacuees were allowed to return home.

Elsewhere in Europe, the heat of battle is far from over: Wildfires have also been raging in Greece and Spain — other countries are...
body.zh: 法国消防队员战胜了大火，近 20 万名疏散人员已返回家园。但欧洲气候引发的野火季节还远未结束。 移动的信号突然来了——大约一分钟左右，消防车就装满了水，飞速驶向远方，尾随一团橙色的尘埃在旋转。 “接到电话时，你总是会感到肾上腺素飙升，”海军陆战队消防员朱利安说。 “但我们受过训练；我们已经做好准备。” 德国之声只能通过军衔和名字确认朱利安大师的身份，他是部署在法国吉伦特省地区的马赛营的一员，该营的任务是扑灭野火，这场野火引发了该国自二战以来最大规模的疏散行动。 大约 264 名消防员在扑灭吉伦特省大火的过程中受伤，其中 4 人丧生。在附近的城镇，法国国旗仍然下半旗以纪念这一损失。 “这一直在我们的脑海中，”另一名海军陆战队消防员达米安中尉解释说，他的团队成员在他身后拖出消防水龙带。 消防员兼医务人员利蒂西亚表示，她试图“不过度打扰”地询问同事的感受。 当被问及影响同事的最常见问题时，她说：“首先是疲劳。” “他们睡得很少。” “你看到这一切了吗？”朱利安师傅一边开车经过路边一排排焦黑的树木和大片焦土，一边指着车窗外问道。 “所有这些都已经被烧毁了。但是你可以看到到处都有小片烟雾。我们绝对必须扑灭这些烟雾，这样火灾就不会重新发生。” 当朱利安在另一个热点地区停下来时，爆发的风险突然成为人们关注的焦点：空气中弥漫着烧焦的味道，天空中弥漫着一团白烟。大约 20 分钟内，浓烟变得又浓又黑，之前已经得到控制的火势在树林中再次熊熊燃烧。 在消防队员身边，有由当地志愿者组成的临时队伍——农民、商人和妇女，他们自己使用拖拉机、货车或四轮四轮车为前线的消防队员运送水，并且经常在没有适当防护装备或训练的情况下亲自冲入大火。 “我们来这里是因为我们需要帮助。”志愿者史蒂文·佩奇（Steven Page）告诉德国之声。朱利安师傅表示，他们发挥了“原始”作用，为消防员节省了“宝贵的时间”。 消防队员说，有时这感觉就像一场“大卫与歌利亚”的战斗。但他们最终脱颖而出。到周六，法国内政部宣布火势不再蔓延。 22万名撤离者中的大多数被允许返回家园。 在欧洲其他地方，战斗的激烈程度还远未结束：希腊和西班牙的野火也在肆虐——其他国家正在……

reflection.en: While we celebrate the heroic efforts of firefighters and the safe return of evacuees, this news reminds us that creation itself groans under the weight of environmental challenges. Yahweh's word acknowledges the deep impact of such struggles, even as we find strength to face ongoing seasons of difficulty.
reflection.zh: 尽管我们为消防员的英勇努力和撤离居民的平安归家而欢欣，但这则新闻提醒我们，受环境挑战的影响，受造界本身仍在叹息。雅伟的话语承认这些挣扎的深远影响，即便我们要在持续的困难季节中寻找力量。

verse.textEn: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.
verse.textZh: 我们知道，一切受造之物一同叹息、劳苦，直到如今。

title.en: Trump holds off new Iran attack, in hope of a swift deal

"Based on this request, I have agreed, for the future benefit of the WORLD and, likewise, the survival of a successful and prosperous Iran, to cancel the attack, subject to being able to rapidly make a DEAL," he said on the post.

title.en: Hungary to shut sole nuclear plant for first time on Sunday
title.zh: 匈牙利将首次关闭其唯一的核电站

summary.en: Record-low water levels on the Danube forced the Paks plant offline, leaving Hungary facing a potential power crunch.
summary.zh: 多瑙河水位创历史新低，迫使匈牙利帕克斯核电站停运，导致该国面临潜在的电力危机。

body.en:
Record-low water levels on the Danube forced the Paks plant offline, leaving Hungary facing a potential power crunch.

Hungary will shut down the Paks nuclear power plant on Sunday for the first time in its 44-year history, Prime Minister Peter Magyar said.

He made the announcement on social media late Saturday night, saying the decision was taken after a further drop in the Danube's water level .

The plant, located 120 kilometers (74.5 miles) south of the capital, Budapest, uses water from the Danube to cool its reactors. It provides more than 40% of Hungary's electricity generation.

The Danube has fallen to record-low levels in some areas after months of below-average rainfall and successive heat waves since May.

Hungary's water authority projected that the Danube, which flows from Germany to the Black Sea, would fall further in the coming days.

It measured the Danube's water level in Budapest at 23 centimeters (9 inches) on Wednesday morning, well below the previous record low of 33 centimeters (13 inches) set in 2018.

As a result, output at the Paks nuclear power plant had already been cut earlier in the week and some reactors shut down.

"Due to a further decline in the Danube's water level, the second-to-last generating unit at the Paks nuclear power plant will be shut down at 1:30 a.m. (2330 GMT)," the prime minister said.

"As a result, the plant is now producing only 240 megawatts (of electricity), and tomorrow (on Sunday), for the first time in 44 years, it will be completely shut down," Magyar added.

The surge in imported electricity prices could cost Hungary between 120 billion and 240 billion forints ($315 million to $630 million, €273 million to €546 million), Tisza Party Vice Chairman Mark Radnai said on Facebook.

Magyar warned the Paks plant could remain offline for weeks and said his government would seek voluntary power cuts from large users, in addition to the 240 megawatts already pledged, with penalties for noncompliance. 

A decree would also allow grid operator MAVIR to mandate consumption cuts and temporarily disconnect large users if necessary.

summary.en: Renowned Nepali mountaineer Nirmal Purja and nine others were tragically killed in an avalanche on Broad Peak, with rescue efforts ongoing to retrieve their bodies.

body.en:
Celebrated Nepali climber Nirmal Purja, who set a record for the fastest ascent of the world's 14 highest mountains, died in an avalanche during an expedition in Pakistan, his company said on Saturday.

"Today it is with profound sadness and immense heartbreak that we confirm that Nirmal 'Nimsdai' Purja tragically lost his life following the avalanche on Broad Peak, his expedition organising company Elite Exped said in an Instagram post.

"We have also received confirmation that other members of the expedition sadly did not survive," it added.

Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah said he was stunned at the deaths of the climbers, including Purja.

"Only physical journey of the climbers has stopped. But the history of their courage, dedication and contributions will always remain alive and inspiring," Shah wrote in a social media post.

Purja, 43, and nine others had been missing since Thursday after being struck by an avalanche on the 8,051-metre Broad Peak, the world's 12th-highest mountain, a technically difficult climb in Pakistan's Gilgit-Baltistan region.

Officials said the bodies of Purja and other climbers were located in a difficult site and had yet to be retrieved.

Purja, who served in the British military with the Gurkhas and later in special forces, completed his record-breaking feat in six months in 2019.

He became widely known internationally after the Netflix documentary chronicling his journey, "14 Peaks: Nothing Is Impossible," was released two years later.

UK defence minister Wes Streeting said he was "incredibly" sad to learn of the death of Purja and the other climbers.

"He was an inspirational man who served in our Armed Forces for many years - and whose incredible mountaineering adventures are known the world over," Streeting wrote on X.

The 10 mountaineers were caught in an avalanche around midday on Thursday. Six of them were Nepalis, and the others were from ⁠Pakistan, Oman, the US and China.

Chhang Dawa Sherpa, a board director of Seven Summit Treks, which had three Sherpa guides among the dead ⁠climbers, said the remaining bodies were "spotted and identified" with the help of drone footage and were yet to be retrieved.

"They are in a difficult spot and have not been retrieved yet," Chhang told Reuters news agency.

He said that unlike Nepal, Pakistan does not have the practice of long-line rescue by helicopters on the mountains.

"We have to take into account the safety of those who go and retrieve the bodies."

Sajid Hussain, deputy director of the tourism department of Gilgit-Baltistan region of Pakistan, said the rescue operation was ongoing.

title.en: How this tiny Spanish city became a global migration flashpoint
title.zh: 这座西班牙小城如何成为全球移民热点

summary.en: Ceuta faced a crisis after tens of thousands of migrants arrived in one day — equivalent to nearly two-thirds of its population.

body.en:
A tiny Spanish territory on the northern tip of Africa has become the focus of international attention — and debate — after more than 50,000 migrants crossed into it in a mass rush that left at least 67 people dead.

The European Union will hold crisis talks after the mass crossing into Ceuta on Thursday. Most of the migrants had returned to Morocco within 48 hours of crossing, but the incident has raised alarm among European leaders about the bloc's shared border security.

Ceuta has steadily fortified its border over the years as it became a key route for migrants trying to reach Europe.

The Spanish exclave already had a border fence with Morocco, but Spanish authorities have since begun installing a 500m-long floating barrier on its sea border with its African neighbour.

It's designed to stand 30 to 70cm above water and extend as much as one metre below the surface, while a channel between the barriers will allow Civil Guard vessels to patrol the area, the government said.

The arrivals were equivalent to nearly two-thirds of Ceuta's permanent population of about 83,000.

Ceuta and Melilla, another Spanish exclave on the North African coast, are the only two land borders between the European Union and Africa.

Many arrivals swam to Ceuta around the Tarajal breakwater — a sea wall extending out from the Spain-Morocco border into the Mediterranean — to come ashore at Tarajal beach.

"Spain gives you the chance to make your future, not like Morocco," Buji, a 21-year-old Moroccan who is studying to be a teacher, told the Associated Press (AP). "I am a talented boy. I just want a chance."

He said he lost his belongings and money in the crossing, and when he realised that he would likely face legal limbo and detention, he turned back.

"I’ve spent perhaps 14 years studying, but there’s nothing at home, and I'd have to work 12-hour shifts for a meagre wage," he told AP.

"That’s why I came here, but I haven’t found any opportunities here either, so I have to go back."

To reach the city, migrants have been known to swim around 5km from the Moroccan town of Fnideq.

Officials said at least 67 bodies were recovered on the Spanish side after some migrants drowned and others were crushed while trying to climb the breakwater and border fence.

Many were driven to migrate by economic hardship and reportedly by rumours circulating on Moroccan social media that border security had been relaxed.

title.en: How does eastern Europe commemorate the Roma Holocaust?
title.zh: 东欧如何纪念罗姆人大屠杀？

summary.en: In 2015, the EU designated August 2 as the European Roma Holocaust Memorial Day. In Germany, the day is marked with memorial services, educational activites and public addresses. And in eastern Europe?
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及智慧、知识与追求真理。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
In 2015, the EU designated August 2 as the European Roma Holocaust Memorial Day. In Germany, the day is marked with memorial services, educational activites and public addresses. And in eastern Europe?

It took decades before Germany recognized the Romani Holocaust — the Nazi genocide of 500,000 European Roma and Sinti during World War II . Several more decades passed before the European Holocaust Memorial Day for Sinti and Roma became an official German and European day of remembrance, celebrated each year on August 2.

Based on initiatives by Polish Roma groups, the Nazi liquidation of the so-called "Gypsy Family Camp" in the Auschwitz-Birkenau Concentration and Extermination Camp on the evening of August 2-3, 1944, was first commemorated half a century later, in 1994. 

Thousands of deported Roma and Sinti had already been killed as a result of malnutrition and disease. That evening, thousands more were forced into gas chambers, shot and beaten to death by Nazi henchmen.

In 2015, the European Parliament declared this date the European Roma Holocaust Memorial Day. In Germany and other European countries, the genocide is commemorated by officials with the participation of government representatives. In some cases, representatives of European governments travel to the memorial site in Auschwitz.

In most cases, however, countries hold their own memorial services — particularly in central and southeastern Europe, where Nazi extermination commonly targeted Romani peoples . These days, such memorial days also take the opportunity to raise awareness for ongoing Antiziganism and the consequences it has. 

Poland , home to an estimated 30,000 Roma, has been observing August 2 since 2011. The ceremony routinely includes a visit by parliamentary and governmental representatives to the Auschwitz Memorial.

Another important day of remembrance is observed each year in the village of Szczurowa, east of Krakow, on July 3. It honors the memory of Polish Roma massacred by German troops in 1943. In 1956, Szczurowa became the first site of a European memorial for victims of the Romani Holocaust.

Other small towns and villages across southeastern Poland also commemorate the killing of Polish Roma during Nazi German occupation. 

In the Czech Republic , where nearly 250,000 Roma live, August 2 has been an official day of remembrance since 2015. The most important ceremony is held in Lety, south of Prague, where Roma organizations have been commemorating the genocide for decades. This is the site where German Nazis established a concentration camp in 1940, and began deporting and imprisoning Romani families from occupied Bohemia from 1942 onward.

title.en: UK court allows plans for Chinese 'super' embassy to advance

summary.en: A UK court has dismissed a legal challenge against Beijing's new embassy in London, which is set to become the largest in the UK. The case, brought by a neighborhood association, had cited security concerns regarding the embassy's presence.

body.en:
A court dismissed a legal challenge against Beijing's new embassy in London, which could become the largest in the UK. The case, brought by a neighborhood association, argued the embassy poses a security threat.

A UK High Court on Friday threw out a challenge against UK authorities' decision to permit a new Chinese super embassy in central London .

The challenge was brought by a neighborhood group called the Royal Mint Court Residents' Association (RMCRA), which represents families and businesses in roughly 100 properties around the planned embassy site.

The RMCRA argued the presence of the embassy could increase the risk of terrorist attacks, lead to the targeting of dissidents and be used to enforce "draconian" Chinese laws in the UK.

The association also claimed that the embassy could pose a fire risk, arguing that Chinese authorities might ignore safety obligations that would be difficult to enforce because of diplomatic immunity on the embassy site.

On that basis, the group argued the development should not have been approved by the UK government as well as the London Borough of Tower Hamlets.

Yet in its ruling on Friday, the High Court said the "RMCRA ​did not produce reasonable ⁠and convincing evidence of the likelihood that a violation of human rights ⁠affecting them ​personally would occur."

In a move that was widely seen as a goodwill gesture toward Beijing, the embassy received approval from the UK government shortly before then-Prime Minister Keir Starmer visited China in January this year. 

 If completed, the new Chinese embassy would be the largest embassy in the UK .

Beijing plans to build the embassy on the site of the former Royal Mint, next to the Tower of London. The site covers around 20,000 square meters (235,000 square feet).

Beijing purchased the property in 2018 for a reported $327 million (€283.9 million), with the intent of relocating its embassy there from its current premises in Portland Place.

In response to the verdict, the RMCRA said it would seek permission to appeal, hoping to take the case to the UK Supreme Court.

"Beijing thinks this judgment is the final word. It isn't. The appeal is already in the works," Luke Pollard, head of the RMCRA, said in a statement.

Activists from  Hong Kong's pro-democracy movement living in exile have also been skeptical of the project, telling DW they fear the embassy could help Beijing suppress dissidents abroad. 

The UK is home to the world's largest Hong Kong diaspora, with an estimated 285,000 people of Hong Kong origin living in the country.

title.en: From petitions to memes: How students made dissent visible
title.zh: 从请愿到网络迷因：学生如何让异议显现

summary.en: Student movements throughout history, from imperial China to modern India, have consistently found new ways to express dissent and challenge established authority, adapting their methods to contemporary tools and symbols.
summary.zh: 从中国古代到当今印度，学生运动不断调整其工具和象征，以挑战权威，使异议得以显现。

body.en:
From imperial China to present-day India, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols of their age to challenge authority.

On July 22, 2026, in rainy Mumbai, India , a casually dressed young woman stepped in front of a slow-moving police van carrying detained students. She placed her palm on the hood, forcing the vehicle to stop.

Mobile phones captured the moment from every angle. She too, raised her own phone and recorded the encounter. Within hours, the clip spread across India and beyond.

It became one of the defining visuals of the Cockroach Janta Party protests, a movement in which students demanded transparency and accountability, following leaks in India's medical entrance exams.

But the power of the moment lay not only in what she did, but in how quickly it was seen. A single gesture, a young woman confronting authority , became a symbol shared across millions of screens.

While the clip belongs to a generation raised on social media, the impulse behind it is much older.

From court petitions and revolutionary posters to photographs, umbrellas and memes, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols available to them, turning them into vehicles for dissent.

Long before television or social media carried dissent across borders, students still found ways to make their grievances heard.

In Eastern Han China, for instance, scholars at the Imperial Academy (Taixue) aligned with reform-minded officials in opposing powerful eunuchs at court, whom many viewed as corrupt and politically overbearing.

They voiced their objections through public criticism, political networks and petitions.

In an era when political communication moved through official channels, petitions were among the established ways of bringing grievances before the throne. Written in formal language and delivered through the bureaucracy, they carried student concerns directly into the state's communication system.

In Paris in 1968, students challenged university authorities and a conservative postwar social order. As demonstrations spread across the French capital and drew in workers, one of the movement's most enduring contributions emerged from a basement workshop at the Ecole des Beaux-Arts.

The Atelier Populaire ("People's Workshop") printed thousands of posters during the protests, many of them overnight. Their bold graphics, silhouettes and slogans became the visual language of the movement. title.en: US-China AI rivalry heats up as Chinese models gain ground

summary.en: China's AI platforms are rapidly advancing, narrowing the gap with US technology. This progress has led to renewed threats from the Trump administration, alongside accusations of intellectual property theft, raising concerns about escalating tensions between the two nations.

body.en:
China's AI platforms are rapidly closing the gap with their US counterparts, prompting fresh threats from the Trump administration. With accusations of intellectual property theft, could tensions boil over?

In what seems like the blink of an eye,  China has gone from being up to five years behind the United States in top-tier artificial intelligence (AI) to lagging by just a few months.

While US players, including Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's ChatGPT , have spent hundreds of billions of dollars to push the frontier of AI, China has pursued a very different path .

Faced with US curbs on high-end chips that help AI to do its most advanced thinking, Chinese tech firms have prioritized dozens of open-source AI models built on "good enough"  technology .

These platforms, including DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen and Xiaomi's MiMo, are now widely deployed across Chinese businesses, government services and consumer devices.

In the latest sign of the gap closing, Chinese startup Moonshot AI last week unveiled Kimi K3, a model that rivals one of the most advanced AI models — Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 — on key benchmarks.

In some tests, Kimi K3 matches or even surpasses Claude with far less computing power and at a fraction of the cost. 

Global technology specialist Alvin W. Graylin thinks Kimi K3's arrival turns high-end AI from an expensive luxury into something practical and affordable.

"For 98% of customers, the 1 to 2% difference [in knowledge] isn't worth paying 10 to 20 times more."

China's latest advance has already drawn a strong reaction from Washington, with US President Donald Trump now threatening to block US access to Chinese AI models.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, meanwhile, warned earlier this week that the US could sanction Chinese models over alleged intellectual property (IP) theft.

Anthropic  and OpenAI have accused Chinese labs of using their models to train their own systems, a process known as distilling.

While distilling is a common practice by AI labs worldwide to a limited extent, the companies say their models have been bombarded with queries to harvest advanced reasoning. The White House warned in April that China was doing it on an "industrial scale."

Beijing has hit back, rejecting the accusations as baseless and calling US threats of sanctions and model bans "technological bullying" to contain China's rise.

Giulia Neaher, a research analyst at the Strategic Foresight Hub at the Washington-based Stimson Center think tank, downplayed the role of distilling in Kimi's progress.

title.en: 'That was crazy': Australia's historic Commonwealth Games day ends with a bizarre twist
title.zh: “这太疯狂了”：澳大利亚历史性的英联邦运动会日以奇异的转折结束

summary.en: A midnight medal ceremony and a scaled-back format made for an unconventional Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The Australian athletics team had its biggest one-day medal haul at the Commonwealth Games on Saturday, ending with a peculiar medal ceremony in a near-empty stadium.

Hours after the Games' athletics program ended, the Aussie men's sprinters were still waiting for their victory to be confirmed after protests over the other podium placings.

When the 4x100 relay team collected their medals in a makeshift ceremony along with the Canadian silver and Nigerian bronze medallists, the clock was ticking towards midnight.

The crowds at Glasgow's Scotstoun Stadium were long gone, with less than a hundred people remaining — mostly made up of Games officials, team staff, journalists and volunteers.

It was an odd ceremony for a major championship, with Australian winner Josh Azzopardi admitting with a smile: "That was crazy! We'd been waiting around not really knowing what was going to happen. It's definitely unique."

"We won gold, felt like it was ages ago now," said his teammate Lachlan Kennedy.

The holdup was the result of Canada's protests over their initial disqualification for a supposed illegal changeover, which was first upheld and then deliberated upon by the jury at great length until Canada was cleared for the silver.

It was an unusual conclusion to Australia's most successful athletics day ever at the Games, with a record haul of seven gold medals and 17 medals in total, including two events where the Aussies swept the podium.

Australia's previous record was set more than 70 years ago, with six gold medals and 11 medals in total in 1950.

It capped off the penultimate day of a stripped-back Games that had been quirky from the outset .

Victoria was originally supposed to host , but withdrew in 2023 due to rising costs. At the time, it prompted some to question the relevance of the Games and whether the event had a future at all.

The following year, organisers announced that Glasgow would step in as host city, with its Games to be supported in part by money from Victoria. The Victorian government had to pay a compensation of $589m including a $380 million settlement to cancel its hosting obligations.

While the Games has always had fewer sports and athletes than the Olympics, the 2026 event was even more pared back.

The 2022 Birmingham Games featured 20 sports and more than 5,000 athletes, while Glasgow hosted just 3,000 athletes competing in ten sports.

Some onlookers said the vibes in the city were vastly different to 2014, when it last hosted the Games.

They didn’t seek the spotlight, but these Northern Territory Police officers found themselves in it.

Sergeant Chris Harden and acting sergeant Karl von Minden were among the investigators who found the body of five-year-old little girl Kumanjayi Little Baby on the outskirts of Alice Springs.

The little girl’s name has been changed for Warlpiri cultural reasons; under Indigenous protocol, it is taboo to speak the name of someone who has died.

The two officers spoke exclusively to SBS News for the first time about the enormous five-day search effort that made international headlines.

It culminated in the discovery of her remains, and within hours the arrest of 49-year-old Jefferson Lewis, who has been charged with her murder.

The two search and rescue specialists were having an extremely busy year. The top end of Australia is flood and cyclone central, and they’d been travelling from disaster to disaster.

Von Minden’s job was to coordinate and oversee the sprawling search operation that involved a call out for volunteers; hundreds arrived, some even flew to Alice Springs to help.

Harden was on the front lines of the grid search, walking metre by metre through buffel grass that had grown high and ominous in the summer rains, wrangling a group of volunteers each day.

"There was holes, washouts, everything which you just could not see," Harden recalled.

"There was a big risk that someone was get bitten by a snake, fall down a hole, do an ankle. But everyone was united. The community were just unbelievable."

Both of them barely slept and neither of them had worked on a search of that scale and complexity before.

"That was quite a unique operation, I think, across the territory. We have coordinated quite large search and rescues before, but never to the scale where we had so many civilian volunteers helping and the amount of people out there and the terrain that we were looking at," von Minden said.

"You go outside and suddenly there's 200 people volunteering, putting their name down, wanting to search," Harden said.

Their police colleagues, the SES, Defence, fire services and all the government agencies and organisations that downed tools on their normal jobs to join forces in the quest to locate the little girl.

"If we didn't have that, yeah, we could still be, you know, searching for her," Harden said.

title.en: 'We committed 7 years ago': SA forges ahead with Indigenous truth-telling commission
title.zh: 南澳州推进原住民真相委员会，称“七年前已承诺”

summary.en: South Australia is proceeding with its Indigenous truth-telling commission, fulfilling a seven-year-old commitment despite the national Voice referendum's failure in 2023.
summary.zh: 尽管2023年全国原住民之声公投失败，南澳大利亚州仍将履行七年前的承诺，继续推进其原住民真相委员会。

body.en:
South Australia will establish an Indigenous Voice to Parliament over coming months, cementing the state as the second-most advanced jurisdiction on the Uluru Statement's unfinished agenda.

Speaking to NITV's John-Paul Janke and Natalie Ahmat on the broadcaster's Garma set against a backdrop of stringybarks rising from the red Arnhem Land dirt, Acting Premier Kyam Maher said the state government would spend $8.5 million on a commission that will run a truth-telling process and advise on a possible treaty.

The commission is the next stage in a program the state's Labor party has pursued since 2019. Responding to the Uluru Statement from the Heart — the 2017 declaration by Indigenous leaders calling for a Voice to Parliament, treaty and truth-telling — was the party's first policy commitment that year. The Labor party is now in government, winning a second election earlier this year.

The Voice to Parliament has since suffered a major setback. In October 2023, just over 60 per cent of Australians rejected a constitutional referendum to recognise Indigenous people and establish a federal advisory Voice to Parliament, with every state and territory except the ACT voting No.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

South Australia though, had already legislated its own Voice to Parliament before the referendum. Maher rejected the argument the No result should halt the state's plans.

"This is about something we committed seven years ago to do in South Australia, and we will take that commitment," he told NITV on Sunday, referencing the 2019 pledge Labor made in opposition and carried into government in 2022.

"What was voted on at the referendum was to change the federal constitution, to firstly recognise Aboriginal people — recognise the oldest living culture this planet's ever seen — but also to establish an advisory body."

He acknowledged not everyone was behind him. "I wouldn't say there's no division," Maher said, adding that the issue still generates dozens of letters to his office each month.

The state's Voice has now been through two elections. The body — elected by and from First Nations South Australians — will advise parliament, cabinet and government agencies on health, education, the criminal justice system and other matters affecting their communities.

Maher said the first part of the state's efforts was spent building the machinery of a body. Without a national precedent, he likened the work to "building the plane as you're flying it".

"[You're] having to put that infrastructure around something that had never happened in Australia before," he said.

body.en:
WARNING: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander readers are advised that this story includes the names and images of Indigenous persons who have passed away.

In December 2025, Australia became the first country to legislate a social media ban for children under the age of 16.

While the jury is still out on its effectiveness , the laws introduced world-first penalties for social media giants that are caught breaking the rules.

Now, a range of countries — including Britain, France and Malaysia — look set to follow suit, something that Australian policymakers have taken as a point of pride.

In late June, the prime minister's office put out a statement saying Australia had "started a global movement". Anthony Albanese himself said the nation was "leading the world".

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

It's not the first time Australia has led the charge on ambitious legislation and inventions.

Lucie Shawcross — who has researched Australian ingenuity and inventiveness at the National Archives of Australia (NAA) — believes "there are just so many incredible [Australian] inventions out there that have made an impact globally".

"Spray-on skin is an Australian invention, the cochlear implant, WiFi," the exhibitions curator told SBS News. "There are some really profound inventions that have impacted upon all of us."

Other distinctly Australian inventions that have seen mass uptake include the dual flush toilet, Hills Hoist, the baby capsule, Aerogard and cask wine (also known as goon ), according to the NAA.

In 2012, Australia took the radical step of removing all branding from cigarette packaging, replacing it instead with plain packaging, public health warnings and confronting images of smoking-related illnesses.

The policy, introduced under Julia Gillard's Labor government, was designed to make smoking less "cool" — or, as Gillard herself wrote in The Guardian in 2013, "kill the glamour and substitute it with the facts: smoking equals death".

The move was widely opposed by cigarette companies who unsuccessfully sued the Australian government over the changes.

By 2016, plain packaging was included in guidelines to the World Health Organisation Framework Convention on Tobacco Control.

Now France, the UK, New Zealand, Norway, Ireland, Thailand, Uruguay, Saudi Arabia, Israel, Slovenia, Türkiye, Canada, Singapore, Belgium, the Netherlands and Georgia have all adopted similar policies.

The approach to North Sullivan's home is a magical journey through winding eucalypt-lined roads, where traffic signs warn of wombats and roaming horses greet passing cars.

The driveway to the 71-year-old's home — aptly named Wombat Gully — is situated on the doorstep of Yengo National Park, part of the World Heritage-listed Greater Blue Mountains area, around two hours north-west of Sydney.

His property is one of 22 clustered in what they call Upper Yango, on the site of a former dairy farm that was subdivided into small hobby farms.

Sullivan says the landholders were a "very disparate community" prior to the Black Summer fires of 2019-20.

But friendships were formed as they fought side-by-side to protect their properties.

From the ashes of that traumatic experience emerged an enduring lesson: one of the most valuable assets in an emergency are the people around you.

The community is now one of many across Australia taking direct action to reduce the risks of fire and flood, as climate change is projected to increase the frequency and severity of such extreme weather events.

Since the fires, the Upper Yango community has developed wide tracks that double as firebreaks in strategic locations, as well as other measures to reduce fire risk to their properties.

However, Sullivan says these efforts are not reflected in their insurance premiums.

He is just one of many landowners SBS News has spoken to in NSW who are either struggling to find insurance cover or facing rising costs.

Some experts warn the pressures could leave some communities unviable, with implications that extend beyond remote and regional Australia.

As premiums continue to rise and access to cover becomes more challenging, communities are questioning whether efforts to reduce disaster risk will be enough to keep insurance affordable.

Professor Paula Jarzabkowski, an expert on insurance protection gaps at the University of Queensland, says there's already significant evidence that many Australians are struggling to get adequate cover for their properties — either because it's too expensive or because policies exclude specific risks, like certain types of flood or fire.

"Brisbane is built on a floodplain, parts of Sydney are built on floodplains, so we have seen catastrophic flooding in these major cities as well," she tells SBS News.

body.en:
For 60 years, Brian Ahmed has farmed the same stretch of land in Melbourne's east. These days, getting past the farm's gate isn't easy — his birds need all the protection they can get.

"At the moment, because of all the concerns with Avian influenza ... I'd say all farms now have increased their biosecurity levels," he told SBS News.

"Our number one priority is to protect our birds, and the best way we can do that is to make sure they don't mix with anyone that they don't need to."

Avian influenza, or bird flu, is a highly contagious virus that predominantly affects bird species, causing severe disease and sudden death.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

It has wreaked havoc on avian and mammal species in other parts of the world, but until recently hadn't made it to mainland Australia.

The disease now appears to be spreading across the country quickly , with 53 confirmed or presumed cases nationwide, just a month after the first contagious bird was found.

The latest figures were confirmed on Saturday, with the Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry saying a silver gull found at Robe in South Australia tested positive for H5 bird flu — the first confirmed detection in a silver gull in Australia.

Experts indicate that the recent detection is important, as gulls move between beaches, wetlands, farmland, and urban areas, potentially spreading the virus to wider environments.

At the same time, in Victoria, preliminary testing has identified five crested terns, three from Portland and two from Nelson Bay, suspected to have bird flu.

Farmers across the country have been encouraged to take precautions, something that might impact their operations.

Chris Groves, chairman of the farming systems committee with the National Farmers Federation, told SBS News that "agricultural industries really have to take their precautions, their biosecurity, to the next level".

"It will cause some interruptions to daily operations of a large poultry farm because they have to be more careful," he said.

"A lot of the big operators, they've prepared for this already. They've dealt with and seen what happened with the other strain of bird flu that we did have in Victoria. So it won't cause a big hiccup in the industry at all there."

There  have been no detections in poultry or in Australia's agricultural production system.

National leaders met on Friday to discuss Australia's ongoing response to the virus, which now spans five states.

title.en: El Niño is already here. But there's still a 'window of opportunity'

summary.en: The El Niño climate pattern has arrived and is projected to be one of the strongest ever recorded, prompting questions about its potential impacts on Australians.
summary.zh: 厄尔尼诺气候模式已经到来，预计将成为有记录以来最强的一次，引发了人们对其可能对澳大利亚人造成影响的疑问。

body.en:
As El Niño strengthens, now is the "window of opportunity" to prepare before its potential impacts unfold, the World Meteorological Organisation (WMO) has warned.

The United Nations agency said El Niño is continuing to intensify and is expected to strengthen from August to October in a new long-range forecast released Saturday.

El Niño typically peaks between November and February, with its greatest influence on global temperatures often felt in the following year.

It's expected to drive up the likelihood of higher-than-normal temperatures across many parts of the world, increasing the risk of drought in some regions and wetter conditions in others.

"El Niño is not just on our doorstep — it is inside the house and turning up the heat," UN Secretary-General António Guterres said.

"And this is only a warm-up act. El Niño is strengthening — adding fuel to a planet already on fire with scorching heat domes, apocalyptic wildfires and record hot seas."

The World Food Programme is seeking to protect 8.8 million people across 22 high-risk countries before weather patterns "escalate into humanitarian emergencies". It expects parts of Africa, Central America and East Asia to be the most at risk.

In Australia, El Niño increases the likelihood of warmer and drier conditions, particularly in the east and southeast, raising the risk of drought and bushfires.

The Bureau of Meteorology (BoM) declared El Niño underway in mid-June, and forecasts it will be a "very strong event" — perhaps among the strongest observed since 1950 — that may persist into autumn next year.

WMO Secretary-General Celeste Saulo urged people and leaders around the world to consider the potential risks to their communities and take action.

"El Niño is one of the most closely monitored climate phenomena in the world," she said.

"This El Niño developing against the backdrop of unprecedented ocean heat and rising temperatures, provides governments and communities with a window of opportunity to anticipate risks and act before impacts unfold."

An El Niño declaration can be particularly concerning for farmers and those in bushfire-prone regions.

While it doesn't guarantee hotter and drier conditions, it does raise the probability that they will occur.

Andrew King, an associate professor of climate science at the University of Melbourne, said that while this El Niño is likely to be one of the strongest on record, a strong El Niño does not necessarily have a huge bearing on Australian climate compared to a weak one.
